html:
The Wardaman are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, in the country southwest of Katherine. The map shows them only in 1815.

Their land of sandstone ranges and savanna holds many rock art sites, among them the Lightning Brothers paintings at Yiwarlarlay, which show two ancestral brothers tied to storms and the wet season. Wardaman elders have also shared a detailed body of star knowledge with outsiders. Their language is not part of the Pama-Nyungan family. Neighbours on the map include the Nungali, the Jaminjung and the Wagiman. The Overland Telegraph Line passed through Katherine in the early 1870s, and cattle stations followed. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
